newsitem.title: USA: Pamela Anderson Lee describes movie sex scenes.
newsitem.headline: Pamela Anderson Lee describes movie sex scenes.

text.p: Former "Baywatch" TV star Pamela Anderson Lee, sued for backing out of a movie deal, told a hushed court Thursday exactly what simulated sex scenes in the film she objected to.
Reading from the script for "Hello, She Lied," Lee read the stage directions for four specific scenes.
"He reaches under her dress; they make passionate love," she read. For another scene she read: "He kisses her breast."
"He picks her up and puts her on the pool table and he gets on top of her," Lee continued in a monotone voice.
"They enjoy a mutually aggressive ... sexual marathon," she said as the court listened intently.
Lee, wearing a mini-skirted, short-sleeved, floral print dress, was called to the stand by her defence, which contends she withdrew from the film project because of objectionable graphic sex scenes.
Cross-examined by the plaintiffs' lawer Robert Wolfe, Lee stated emphatically: "You will never see me in another simulated sex scene for the rest of my life.

"I don't want to be touched by people I don't know," she said. "I have that right. If I had gone to Florida (to shoot the film) they would have made me do simulated sex -- I know that, I'm not stupid."
"Do you honestly think I should have done this movie? If I were your daughter would you want me to do it?" she asked Wolfe.
When he pressed her about on-screen lovemaking and simulated sex, Lee became exasperated.
"I don't even know what you're asking me ... Ask me a real question," she snapped.
Judge David Horowitz adjourned the session for a lunch break before Wolfe could continue.
Later he continued his line of questioning, asking the actress: "Isn't it true, you can do lovemaking without nudity?"
"I've had a lot of experience in this area -- I don't kow if you have," she shot back testily at the lawyer as the plaintiffs wound up her cross-examination.

Lee is being sued for $5 million by The Private Movie Co., which alleges she broke an agreement to star in "Hello, She Lied" because she was offered $500,000 to make the feature film "Barb Wire", which was a box-office flop.
The Canadian-born actress, who is married to rock drummer Tommy Lee of the band Motley Crue, claimed she changed her mind about making "Hello, She Lied" after seeing the script.
In testimony last week she told the court that although she was not opposed to nudity, she did object to graphic sex scenes in the script.
Even when a proposed naked shower scene was rewritten because of her complaints, she said, it was replaced with a scene in which her character was to have sex on a pool table.
"Hello, She Lied" was later made as "Miami Hustler" with model Kathy Ireland in the lead role for the Showtime cable TV channel. Ireland had a "no-nudity" clause in her contract.
Closing arguments are expected on Monday, with Judge Horowitz announcing his verdict in the non-jury trial later next week.
